Definition: the orifice of the womb (from which the fetus breaks forth)
BiblicalUsage: The word is the breaking forth, the opening of the womb, and Hezekiah uses it in his darkest hour: the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth. Hosea turns it into judgment: Ephraim is an unwise son who will not stay in the place of the breaking forth of children.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is of a crisis that cannot deliver itself: the birth is ready and the strength is gone, and only God can bring it forth.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
